title: Why Large? Tiny LMs & Agents on Edge/Robotics — Cormac Brick, Google
talk_summary: Cormac Brick of Google's AI Edge team surveys small (1-4B) and tiny (50-500M) language models for on-device deployment, covering quantization, runtimes, and fine-tuning playbooks. The core transferable idea is that narrow, single-task work can be done by much smaller fine-tuned models trained on synthetically generated data, achieving comparable quality at far lower cost and latency.

takeaways.technique: Fine-tune tiny models for narrow fixed tasks instead of routing everything to large models
takeaways.what_they_do: For a single well-defined task (function calling, summarization, proofreading), they fine-tune a 270-500M parameter model on synthetic data and get quality equal to or better than a 2-4B general model, at much higher speed and lower memory.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you're willing to put the time and energy into creating a synthetic data set and fine-tuning a model you can achieve a similar like the same or greater quality with a model that is much much smaller
takeaways.numbers: 270M-500M param fine-tuned models; 45 tokens/sec decode vs single-digit for 2B on Raspberry Pi; 86%+ reliability on 10-function calling task

takeaways.technique: Synthetic data generation to fine-tune for a fixed task
takeaways.what_they_do: They synthetically generate 10k-10M samples to fine-tune a small model to high reliability for a specific task, and open-sourced the dataset (mobile_actions) so others can reproduce it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: in the range of 10,000 to 10 million samples of synthetically generated um data will be sufficient to fine-tune a smaller model to a really really high degree of reliability

takeaways.technique: Aggressive quantization to shrink model footprint
takeaways.what_they_do: They mix 2-bit, 4-bit, and 8-bit quantization plus per-layer embeddings to get a 2B model down to ~2.9 bits per weight, ~841MB of weights.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it uses a mix of like two bit, four bit and 8 bit quantization getting it down to like I know like 2.9 bits per weight
takeaways.numbers: ~2.9 bits/weight; 841MB weights for 2B text model; ~2GB active RAM with KV cache

takeaways.technique: Zero-shot prompting suffices for small general models on simple tasks
takeaways.what_they_do: For 1-4B models, they report zero-shot prompting gets good performance and is somewhat robust at function calling and agent skills, so no fine-tuning needed if the task fits.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can just kind of use zero soft prompting and get pretty good performance. Also to use Laura adapters and it's kind of somewhat robust at doing things like kind of function calling and agent skills
